title: The power of expectation
text: Sugar pills contain no medicine, yet when patients believe in them, real things happen in the body. title: A superorganism underground
text: An ant colony behaves in many ways like a single animal: the queen lays eggs, but the colony's big {{1}} — where to forage, when to move house, which invaders to attack — are made collectively, though no ant issues orders and no committee ever meets. title: The dance of the bees
text: When a honeybee finds a field of flowers, it returns to the hive and {{1}} a dance on the vertical comb. title: Seeing with sound
text: Shout into a canyon and the echo comes back; a bat has simply turned that accident into a {{1}}. title: The octopus problem
text: Of all the puzzles in the sea, the octopus may be the most {{1}}: a mollusc, related to clams and snails, that behaves like something from another planet. title: Why ice floats
text: Almost every substance is denser as a solid than as a liquid, so its solid form simply {{1}} in its own melt. Water, mercifully, is the exception: ice floats. title: The crust of flavour
text: Much of what we call cooking is really one chemical reaction, first {{1}} in 1912 by the French doctor Louis-Camille Maillard. title: Navigators with feathers

title: The key that cracked the hieroglyphs
text: For fourteen centuries the writing of ancient Egypt was a closed book: nobody could {{1}} hieroglyphs, and the civilisation that built the pyramids kept its thoughts to itself. title: Out of the ashes
text: The Great Fire of London began in the small hours of 2 September 1666, in the bakery on Pudding Lane, and for three days it {{1}} through the wooden city unchecked. text: The Silk Road was never a single road, and silk was never its only cargo. title: The machine that changed everything
text: By 1450 a skilled scribe could copy perhaps two books a year, and a single volume could cost as much as a house. title: A canal between two oceans
text: A ship passing through the Panama Canal climbs, in effect, a flight of stairs. title: A world in a leaf

title: Time by the railway
text: Before the railways, every town kept its own sun. Noon in Bristol arrived a quarter of an hour after noon in London, and nobody minded: time was local, {{1}} by sundials and habit. title: Confidently wrong
text: The less competent people are, the less likely they are to know it — a finding that has entered popular culture as the Dunning-Kruger effect. title: Cities five degrees hotter
text: On the hottest afternoons of summer, a city can run five degrees warmer than the countryside around it. title: A fridge at the end of the world
text: Halfway between mainland Norway and the North Pole, a concrete doorway {{1}} into a mountainside. title: The vanishing night

title: The map in your pocket
text: The map in your pocket knows where you are to within a few metres, and it {{1}} the strange arithmetic of Einstein to do it. title: Roll the dice again

title: A run for everyone
